characters.name: Saint Augustine
characters.description: Narrator and author of the Confessions; Christian theologian and Bishop of Hippo recounting his life and conversion

characters.name: God
characters.description: The Lord, the divine addressee of Augustine's prayers and reflections

characters.name: Jesus Christ
characters.description: Referred to as the Son, Savior and Mediator; central to Augustine's conversion and theology

characters.name: Holy Spirit
characters.description: The Paraclete/Comforter; divine Spirit discussed as active, 'borne over the waters' and given to believers

characters.name: Augustine's mother
characters.description: Augustine's pious mother (unnamed in the supplied text), a central figure in his conversion through prayer and care

aliases.text: that chaste, godly, and sober widow

characters.name: Patricius
characters.description: Augustine's father (referred to by name in the text); a pagan/slow-to-believe figure in Augustine's youth

characters.name: Alypius
characters.description: Close friend and companion of Augustine; friend in study and conversion, later a fellow Christian

characters.name: Nebridius
characters.description: Friend of Augustine, thoughtful seeker after truth who accompanies Augustine in parts of his intellectual journey

characters.name: Ambrose
characters.description: Ambrose of Milan, Bishop and influential preacher whose sermons and example play a key role in Augustine's conversion

characters.name: Simplicianus
characters.description: Simplicianus, a senior Christian and mentor figure (Ambrose's elder), who counsels Augustine

characters.name: Verecundus
characters.description: An acquaintance and grammarian of Milan who hosts Augustine and friends; described as constrained by obligations

characters.name: Faustus
characters.description: Faustus, a Manichaean bishop (renowned among Manichees) whom Augustine consults and finds intellectually limited

characters.name: Victorinus
characters.description: Victorinus, a Roman rhetorician who converted to Christianity; Augustine cites his conversion as an example of grace

characters.name: Pontitianus
characters.description: An African official at the imperial court whose telling of Antony the monk and desert examples prompts Augustine's decisive turn

characters.name: Firminus
characters.description: Friend and interlocutor of Augustine; related anecdotes (father's consultation of astrologers) influence Augustine's rejection of astrology

characters.name: Romanianus
characters.description: A wealthy townsman and friend who supports Augustine and companions; discussed in relation to communal plans

characters.name: Euodius
characters.description: Friend from Augustine's city who joins Augustine's household and partakes in his spiritual life and song

characters.name: Adeodatus
characters.description: Augustine's son, born to him before his conversion, depicted as gifted and beloved; raised with Augustine after conversion

characters.name: Gervasius
characters.description: One of two martyrs (with Protasius) whose relics Ambrose uncovers at Milan; their discovery is narrated by Augustine

characters.name: Protasius
characters.description: One of the pair of martyrs (with Gervasius) whose bodies are discovered and venerated at Milan

characters.name: Justina
characters.description: Justina, mother of Emperor Valentinian; mentioned as an Arian sympathizer who vexed Bishop Ambrose

characters.name: Valentinian
characters.description: Emperor Valentinian (referenced in relation to Justina and court matters)

characters.name: Antony
characters.description: Antony the Egyptian (St. Antony), the desert monk whose life Augustine hears about and who inspires conversions

characters.name: Cyprian
characters.description: Saint Cyprian (referenced via an oratory in his memory where Augustine's mother waits)

characters.name: Paul (the Apostle)
characters.description: The Apostle Paul, scripturally cited and prayed with; Augustine cites Pauline teaching and letters

characters.name: Abraham
characters.description: Biblical patriarch cited by Augustine in theological argument

characters.name: Isaac
characters.description: Biblical patriarch cited in Augustine's discussion of types and scriptural interpretation

characters.name: Jacob
characters.description: Biblical patriarch invoked in Augustine's theological reflections

characters.name: Moses
characters.description: Moses, the scriptural lawgiver; Augustine discusses the interpretation of Mosaic texts

characters.name: David
characters.description: King David, author of Psalms; Augustine frequently references and sings David's psalms

characters.name: Solomon
characters.description: Biblical figure (King Solomon) referenced by Augustine in exegesis and example

characters.name: Esau
characters.description: Biblical figure (Esau) cited in moral examples

characters.name: Jacob (as sibling pair with Esau)
characters.description: Biblical figure (Jacob) appearing in Augustine's ethical examples

characters.name: Dido
characters.description: Literary character from Virgil's Aeneid referenced as an object of Augustine's youthful curiosities

characters.name: Aeneas
characters.description: Trojan hero of Virgil's Aeneid referenced in Augustine's account of studying poetry

characters.name: Pylades
characters.description: Classical figure referenced alongside Orestes as an example of mutual devotion

characters.name: Orestes
characters.description: Classical figure cited with Pylades as an example of mutual willingness to die for one another

characters.name: Jove/Jupiter
characters.description: Roman god (Jove/Jupiter) referenced in Augustine's critique of pagan literature

characters.name: Anubis
characters.description: Egyptian deity mentioned as an example of pagan idolatry Augustine critiques

characters.name: Terence
characters.description: Classical playwright referenced by Augustine in discussion of grammar and morals

characters.name: Virgil
characters.description: Roman poet (Virgil) referenced for Augustine's youthful studies

characters.name: Homer
characters.description: Ancient Greek poet (Homer) mentioned as part of Augustine's early literary curriculum

characters.name: Cicero (Tully)
characters.description: Roman orator and author (referred to as Tully) whose work 'Hortensius' greatly influenced Augustine

characters.name: Seneca
characters.description: Roman philosopher and writer mentioned among authors Augustine read

characters.name: Hippocrates
characters.description: Ancient medical authority cited in discussion of faculty and learning

characters.name: Catiline
characters.description: Historical Roman figure (Catiline) invoked in rhetorical example
